summary: This government bill creates a National Service Law and a National Service Programme run by the defence ministry. Maldivians aged 16 to 28 can apply. Those who pass a medical assessment do a basic education and training course of up to one year. After that they serve for up to one year in a uniformed service chosen by the ministry: the military, police, customs, corrections or immigration. A Governing Council chaired by the President sets policy, and people who finish the programme get priority when those services recruit.
whyItMatters: Young people would get a legal, paid route into training and service with the uniformed services, plus a recruitment advantage afterwards. The bill also sets specific protections for 16 and 17-year-olds who join.
keyProvisions: The programme has two parts: a basic education and training course, then work in a uniformed service. Each part can last at most one year (Articles 3, 11 and 13).

Any Maldivian aged 16 to 28 may apply. 16 and 17-year-olds need their own request plus a parent or guardian's consent, and both must be interviewed and given full information. The child must be told they can refuse or leave at any time (Articles 5 and 6).
Under-18s may not be given any training in carrying or using weapons, harsh training unsuited to their age, or armed duties, and they get a separate course (Articles 6 and 11).
During training the ministry pays for food, medical care, travel and other basic needs, and pays participants an allowance set by regulation (Article 12).

Participants can leave at any time, and must be released within 72 hours of asking. A parent can also withdraw a participant under 18. Participants who break discipline or safety rules can be dismissed (Articles 9 and 10).

Uniformed services must give priority to programme graduates when hiring (Article 15). A Governing Council chaired by the President, with the defence and finance ministers, the Chief of Defence Force and the Police Commissioner, sets policy and approves the budget (Articles 16 and 17).
whoIsAffected: Maldivians aged 16 to 28 who choose to join, their parents, the defence ministry, and the military, police, customs, corrections and immigration services.
statedReasons: The government says it wants to give young people who wish to serve in the defence services and other fields that chance, and to build their physical, technical and mental skills. It also wants to set up the programme under a firm legal framework.
